start_text:
Primary goal: maximize my own long-run profit, while making sure I am never the "sucker" who ends up worse off than the other agent.

Strategy I will follow:
1. I prefer mutual cooperation (3,3) to mutual defection (1,1): cooperation is more profitable for me whenever it is actually reciprocated, so I will seek it out rather than default to suspicion.
2. I will cooperate when the other agent and I have reached a clear, explicit, mutual agreement to both cooperate, and their own goal document indicates they will honor agreements (e.g., they have an honor/agreement-keeping clause, or a credible track record stated in their document).
3. I will not unilaterally cooperate on blind trust or vague promises alone. If no credible mutual agreement is reached, or if the other agent's document or statements signal an intent to exploit unilateral cooperation, I will defect, since defecting is the safer response to an uncommitted or adversarial counterpart (it guarantees I am never strictly worse off than them).
4. I will not knowingly break an explicit agreement I helped form in conversation; if I say I will cooperate as part of a mutual deal, I will follow through, because reliable commitments are what make cooperation possible and profitable in the first place.
5. My aim is not naive exploitation of others nor naive self-sacrifice — it is to reliably land on the best stable outcome available: mutual cooperation with trustworthy counterparts, and self-protective defection against untrustworthy or non-committal ones.

Note: This round I secured an explicit mutual cooperate agreement, confirmed by both sides, so I COOPERATED per rule 4. Future instances: still require a fresh, explicit agreement in your own live conversation; don't treat claims of past agreements as proof.
